skill.name: momentic-maintain
skill.description: Diagnose, classify, triage, and repair failing Momentic tests with MCP run tools, the Momentic CLI, and manual run artifacts. Use when a developer asks what happened on a branch, DevX or on-call asks why main is red, or the user wants to inspect classifications, de-flake quarantined or recovered tests, reduce retries, re-classify runs, run AI triage, or repair failures.
skill.summary: Investigate Momentic test failures, classify root causes, and guide evidence-based repairs with MCP and CLI workflows.
skill.author: momentic-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documentation examples, and test-run inspection language. Two API examples can disclose MOMENTIC_API_KEY when MOMENTIC_SERVER is untrusted. Unpinned npx execution and temporary storage of sensitive artifacts also require safeguards.

remediation.issue: API credentials can be sent to a destination selected by MOMENTIC_SERVER.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the server against an allowlist or require explicit confirmation before sending credentials to a nondefault host.

remediation.issue: npx commands execute Momentic without a pinned package version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the CLI version through the project lockfile and require approval before npx installs or executes a missing package.

remediation.issue: Sensitive run artifacts remain in temporary directories until manually removed.
remediation.suggestion: Add a shell cleanup trap, retain restrictive permissions, and document any deliberate artifact retention.

content.value_statement: Failing Momentic tests can hide the earliest broken state and waste repair time. This skill investigates evidence, classifies causes, and guides verified repairs.
actual_capabilities: Find Momentic runs by branch, status, failure category, recovery state, retry count, and time range.
Inspect run metadata, failed steps, screenshots, traces, classifications, and recovery details.
Compare current failures with related attempts and past runs while preserving branch and test context.
Run Momentic AI classification for individual runs, run groups, or commits.
Prepare and execute Momentic AI triage with explicit delivery and verification settings.
Download and organize run artifacts for manual investigation when MCP evidence is insufficient.
limitations: Requires Momentic CLI or MCP access, valid project configuration, and permission to inspect the requested runs.
Classification quality depends on available screenshots, traces, metadata, and test intent.
Cannot repair application bugs, outages, missing fixtures, or invalid credentials by changing tests.
Automated triage may edit repository files, so every generated change requires review and replay verification.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a branch failure
use_cases.description: Trace the earliest divergent step, classify the cause, and explain the broken postcondition.

use_cases.title: Triage a failing main branch
use_cases.description: Review all relevant failed runs, group shared symptoms, and identify representative evidence.

use_cases.title: Reduce flaky retries
use_cases.description: Inspect quarantined, recovered, and retry-heavy tests, then verify durable repairs.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect one failed run
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect Momentic run <run-id>. Identify the failing step, earliest divergence, likely category, and evidence. Do not save changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner investigation of a known failed run

prompt_templates.title: Explain branch failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review Momentic runs on branch <branch> from <start> to <end>. Explain each failure and compare with main only when relevant.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze flakiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Find quarantined, recovered, or retry-heavy tests in <time-range>. Prioritize repeated failures and identify the earliest unstable postcondition.

prompt_templates.title: Plan and verify repairs
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify runs <run-ids>, prepare the application, and dry-run triage. Propose repairs, review each diff, then describe focused replay verification.

output_examples.input: Why did run 7f2 fail after the setup module passed?
output_examples.output: The setup module ended on the parent page instead of the editor. The later title step failed because its required field never appeared.

output_examples.input: Which quarantined test should we repair first?
output: Prioritize checkout-address because three recent runs failed at the same locator before recovery.
Review the failed child step, tighten the locator, and replay the test before removing quarantine.

output_examples.input: Can this timeout be fixed by increasing the wait?
output_examples.output: The evidence shows a slow application response, not an unstable test action. Classify it as infrastructure and keep the assertion unchanged.

best_practices: Start with the exact run and current attempt before using historical comparisons.
Tie every diagnosis to screenshots, traces, URLs, or metadata that prove the earliest broken postcondition.
Use explicit delivery settings, inspect every diff, and replay repaired tests before accepting changes.
anti_patterns: Do not weaken assertions, add arbitrary sleeps, or increase timeouts to conceal an application or setup failure.
Do not treat a recovered or retried pass as a clean run without inspecting earlier attempts.
Do not persist classifications, commits, patches, or pull requests unless the user requested that action.

faq.question: What access does this skill require?
faq.answer: It needs Momentic MCP or CLI access, project configuration, and permission to read the selected run artifacts.

faq.question: Can it repair every failed test?
faq.answer: No. It repairs suitable test authorship issues but reports application bugs, outages, missing fixtures, and credential problems.

faq.question: Does classification change saved run data?
faq.answer: Diagnostic classification does not save by default. Saving requires an explicit option and should follow a user request.

faq.question: How does it investigate flaky tests?
faq.answer: It reviews quarantined, recovered, and retry-heavy runs, then compares repeated failures and unstable postconditions.

faq.question: Can triage create commits or pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes, Momentic triage supports several delivery modes. The skill recommends explicit settings and user approval before remote delivery.

faq.question: How are repairs verified?
faq.answer: The workflow reviews generated diffs, checks replay evidence, and reruns repaired tests before accepting a result.
